verdicts.note: 21 years in the office [S1][S5], operations commander from 2019 and chief deputy running patrol, major crimes and internal investigations [S6][S7], running to 'build on our history' [S1][S2]. Not the incumbent, but four sources on long tenure support -2 high as the maximal record case in this race.

Response coverage, investigations, casework for prosecutors and 'hold offenders accountable' [S1][S3] are pole_a; body cameras and constitutional-rights language [S1] temper it, and there is no encampment or mandatory-treatment plank, so -1 not -2.

Not evidence on the reform axis as the rubric defines it (work within party/donor structures vs refuse PAC money, term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy). Continuity with the office under the last two sheriffs [S1][S2] is office continuity, already reflected on experience.

Rancher and retired fire chief with no stated law enforcement experience [S1], against a 21-year chief deputy. Fire-chief service is public experience, but none in this office or field; pamphlet-only evidence is properly reflected in medium.

Not evidence on the reform axis as the rubric defines it (work within party/donor structures vs refuse PAC money, term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy). 'Full and open transparency, constitutional rights and community engagement' so the office could 'better serve us' [S1] is about sheriff's-office conduct, not political money or structure.
